question: Does a continuous full-family margin improve over an integer minimum vote, or over one mask, when the upstream selector, candidate width and proposal generator are replaced together? This is a second pipeline on the same previously used sources. No outcomes on these new slates were inspected at design.
splits: Ten-task and six-wide panels keep their original 30 and 16 fold layouts, fitting/proposal/guard/outer rows, preprocessing, rare flag and equal-task weighting. Keep the panels separate. No extra task/exclusion/learner/hyperparameter after observing the outcomes.
anchor_and_slate: Rank all columns by univariate ANOVA F from fitting rows only after fit-partition median imputation. Put undefined constant scores below all defined scores, resolve equal scores by column index. The anchor is the best max(2,ceil(d/2)) columns bounded by d. Drop max(1,floor(anchor_width/4)) columns. Candidate 1 is the top retained prefix. Other candidates each exchange exactly one prefix column with one of the remaining anchor columns. Sample up to seven distinct pairs uniformly without replacement in prefix-rank by other-rank order, using numpy default_rng with SeedSequence([87201, UCI source id, fold]); use every pair when there are at most seven. Sort the resulting candidates by summed within-anchor F ranks then lexicographic column indices for tie resolution. Restorations may use the outside-anchor tail in F order with the original separating family.
learners: The masking predictor and reduced/full receiving learner both use the same previously specified random forest settings as forest_cross.json, new support fits with the same seeds, start anew at each stage. Preserve existing original and bootstrap panel weights, metric margins, relative guard and outer tolerances. Compare F-prefix, exact uniform over slate, ordinal minimum, full continuous minimum over the identical family, one empty-restoration point margin. Fixed unrounded ties and one nominal candidate per policy. If an anchor were singleton, return it.
endpoint: Primary coupled full minus ordinal mean guarded safe compression U, with breach risk reported alongside, separately by cohort. Always include full minus point, full minus uniform, point minus vote, ordinal minus prefix, point minus prefix. Secondary guard-free version delivers the same prechosen candidate without the guard, and is scored against the same receiver anchor. Cross-pipeline differences describe the bundle of changes, not causal effects of an individual design choice.
reporting: Record real predictions for every anchor and candidate and every guard, all nominee scores/masks and training time. Commit the selections and raw probabilities before opening this pipeline's outer scores. Count marginal ties, indicator equivalence, nomination discordance, realized returns, equal-task paired 30000 percentile bootstrap (seed 33119), number and identity of contributing tasks. One hour per fold. Report any incomplete units, all costs as machine-specific. No choice between pipelines based on the current outcomes.
